notable.name: Sami languages
notable.note: regional/minority official status in parts of the north (Sápmi)

language.script: Latin (ä, ö, å — note: uses ä/ö rather than Norwegian/Danish's æ/ø, a precise spelling-based way to tell them apart)

terrainDescription.zh: 北部為廣大針葉林與湖泊地帶，西北與挪威交界處漸轉山地，南部斯科訥地區則有較平坦的農業平原。
terrainDescription.en: Extensive boreal forest and lakes dominate the north, rising to mountains near the Norwegian border in the northwest, while the southern Skåne region has flatter agricultural plains.

plate.color: white background, black text, blue EU band with "S" on the left

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Black-and-white, wedge-shaped, round, or thin-and-curved, typically with a grey reflector (orange near intersections); highway outer lines look solid from a distance but are actually broken into small sections — a subtle difference from Finland's/Norway's more solid-looking lines; roadside snow poles are orange with a tall white reflector slightly above the pole's middle, sometimes with a second thinner reflector above

utilityPole.transformerMount: Not strongly documented for Sweden specifically — likely a similar Nordic wooden-pole style to Norway's, but treat as inferred rather than confirmed

historicalContext.zh: 瑞典語、挪威語、丹麥語同屬北日耳曼語族，書面文字高度相通，但瑞典語使用 ä、ö（而非挪威語/丹麥語的 æ、ø），是精確區分三者的可靠拼字線索；薩米語在北部薩普米地區具地區官方地位。
historicalContext.en: Swedish, Norwegian, and Danish are all North Germanic languages with largely mutually intelligible writing, but Swedish uses ä/ö rather than Norwegian/Danish's æ/ø — a precise, reliable spelling-based way to tell them apart. Sami languages hold regional official status in the northern Sápmi area.
